genres.Alt. Rock: Guitar-driven rock with indie or college-radio roots; often moody or melodic rather than mainstream arena rock.
genres.Blues: African-American tradition built on bent notes, call-and-response, and 12-bar forms; ancestor to rock and R&B.
genres.Country: Story songs with fiddle, steel guitar, and Southern/U.S. rural imagery; strong verse-chorus hooks.
genres.Disco: Four-on-the-floor drums, orchestral hits, and dance-club grooves; peak in the late 1970s.
genres.EDM: Electronic dance music: synthesizers, drops, and DJ-led builds aimed at clubs and festivals.
genres.Folk: Acoustic storytelling and traditional song shapes; often fingerpicked guitar and plainspoken lyrics.
genres.Funk: Syncopated bass lines, tight drums, and rhythmic guitar; danceable and groove-first.
genres.Gospel: Church-rooted harmony, hand-claps, and uplifting or spiritual themes influencing soul and pop.
genres.Jazz: Improvisation, extended harmony, and swing or modal rhythms; big band to small-combo styles.
genres.Metal: Heavy distorted guitars, loud drums, and high-energy vocals; subgenres span thrash to glam.
genres.Pop: Short hooks, polished production, and broad radio appeal; verse-chorus focus and memorable melodies.
genres.Punk: Fast tempos, simple chords, and rebellious attitude; raw sound with short, direct songs.
genres.R&B: Rhythm and blues: soulful vocals, groove pockets, and influence from gospel and funk.
genres.Rap: Rhythmic speech over beats; emphasis on flow, wordplay, and sampled or programmed production.
genres.Reggae: Offbeat guitar chops, bass-led grooves, and Caribbean roots; laid-back but syncopated.
genres.Rock: Electric guitars, drums, and bass in song forms from classic rock to hard rock.
genres.SKA: Upstroke guitar, brass punches, and Jamaican dance rhythms; often upbeat and horn-heavy.
genres.Today: Catch-all chart label for current-era tracks that do not map cleanly to older genre bins.
genres.World: Non-Western or hybrid traditions: regional instruments, scales, and rhythms in a pop context.
